analysis.investment_thesis: Elgi Equipments has a genuinely compelling global expansion narrative — building a world-class air compressor brand from Coimbatore to Europe, Australia, and North America — and net profit CAGR of 23.9% over 9 years is respectable. But revenue has grown at only 10.7% CAGR, a 42x P/E and 32x EV/EBITDA already price in a future growth story that the underlying numbers have not yet delivered.
key_strengths: Credible global brand-building: international revenue presence across 22+ countries with expanding distribution, a rare achievement for an Indian industrial company
Operating profit CAGR of 17.2% over 9 years — faster than revenue — signals genuine margin leverage and improving product mix toward premium compressors
ROE of 20.1% and ROCE of 21.9% at/above Fisher's thresholds; FCF has been positive for 5 consecutive years (INR 298 Cr in FY25)
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of 10.7% does not justify a 42x trailing P/E; even Fisher's generous valuation tolerance requires 20%+ growth to underpin premium multiples
Operating margin of only 12.22% is thin for a premium industrial goods company — pricing power is not yet fully established in competitive export markets against Atlas Copco and Ingersoll Rand
FY24 net profit fell to INR 312 Cr from INR 371 Cr in FY23, then recovered to INR 350 Cr in FY25 — earnings trajectory is inconsistent
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 32x is extraordinarily expensive for an industrial machinery company with 10-11% revenue growth — the stock is pricing in a step-change in global market share that may take a decade to arrive
Debt has risen to INR 528–577 Cr range while operating cash generation (INR 391 Cr in FY25) only modestly exceeds capex (INR 95 Cr) plus dividend; international expansion capex could pressure FCF
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have enormous respect for Elgi's ambition — their 'To Be the Best' global compressor strategy is the kind of long-term, management-driven vision that I look for in a Fisher holding. The evidence that they can execute internationally is real: revenue has nearly tripled since 2016 and the operating profit has grown 4x, reflecting both market share gains and the operational leverage of a global manufacturing platform.

However, my discipline requires that I distinguish between a great business and a great investment. At 42x trailing P/E, the market is already paying for 10 years of optimistic outcomes. The gap between Elgi's current 12.22% operating margin and the 18–20% margins of global leaders like Atlas Copco or Kaeser is where the real story lies — if management can close that gap through product premiumisation and service revenue, the stock will reward patient holders. Until I see consistent revenue growth above 15% and margin expansion toward 15%+, I treat this as a HOLD at current prices.
